bottom_line: In patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by left ventricular dysfunction and heart failure, eplerenone vs placebo reduced death from any cause (relative risk, 0.85; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.75 to 0.96; P=0.008).
implications: These data support that, over a mean follow-up of 16 months, eplerenone (vs placebo) in addition to optimal medical therapy reduced all-cause mortality (relative risk, 0.85; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.75 to 0.96; P=0.008) and reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for cardiovascular events (relative risk, 0.87; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.79 to 0.95; P=0.002). The results also show increased serious hyperkalemia (5.5 percent vs 3.9 percent; P=0.002), so the findings do not establish net benefit without considering this reported safety tradeoff.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial design in post–acute myocardial infarction patients.
major_points.quote: We conducted a multicenter, international, random- ized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

major_points.text: Intervention dosing: 25 mg daily initially with titration to a maximum of 50 mg daily.
major_points.quote: Patients were randomly assigned to eplerenone (25 mg per day initially, titrated to a maximum of 50 mg per day; 3313 patients) or placebo (3319 patients)

major_points.text: Primary endpoints included all-cause death and a cardiovascular composite (CV death or hospitalization for CV events).
major_points.quote: The two primary end points were time to death from any cause and time to death from cardiovascular causes or first hospitalization for a cardiovascular event

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with eplerenone than placebo.
major_points.quote: there were 478 deaths in the eplerenone group and 554 deaths in the placebo group (relative risk, 0.85; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.75 to 0.96; P=0.008).

major_points.text: The cardiovascular composite primary endpoint (CV death or hospitalization for CV events) was reduced with eplerenone.
major_points.quote: The rate of the other primary end point, death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for cardiovascular events, was reduced by eplerenone (relative risk, 0.87; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.79 to 0.95; P=0.002)

major_points.text: Sudden death from cardiac causes was reduced with eplerenone.
major_points.quote: There was also a reduc- tion in the rate of sudden death from cardiac causes (relative risk, 0.79; 95 percent con- fidence interval, 0.64 to 0.97; P=0.03).

major_points.text: Serious hyperkalemia was more frequent with eplerenone than placebo.
major_points.quote: The rate of serious hyperkalemia was 5.5 percent in the eplerenone group and 3.9 percent in the placebo group (P=0.002)

major_points.text: Hypokalemia was less frequent with eplerenone than placebo.
major_points.quote: the rate of hypokalemia was 8.4 percent in the eplerenone group and 13.1 percent in the placebo group (P<0.001).

inclusion_criteria.text: Eligible for randomization 3 to 14 days after acute myocardial infarction.
inclusion_criteria.quote: were eligible for randomization 3 to 14 days after acute myocardial infarction

inclusion_criteria.text: Left ventricular dysfunction documented by LVEF 40% or lower measured after the index acute myocardial infarction and before randomization.
inclusion_criteria.quote: left ventricular dysfunction as documented by a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40 percent or lower on echocardiography, radionuclide angiog- raphy, or angiography

inclusion_criteria.text: Heart failure documented by pulmonary rales, chest radiography showing pulmonary venous congestion, or a third heart sound.
inclusion_criteria.quote: heart failure as documented by the presence of pulmonary rales, chest radiography showing pulmonary venous congestion, or the pres- ence of a third heart sound.

inclusion_criteria.text: In patients with diabetes who met criteria for left ventricular dysfunction after acute myocardial infarction, symptoms of heart failure did not have to be demonstrated.

exclusion_criteria.quote: a serum creatinine concentration of more than 2.5 mg per deciliter (220 µmol per liter)

criticisms.text: Trial not designed with sufficient power to draw statistical conclusions about individual subgroups; caution advised interpreting subgroup analyses.
criticisms.quote: our trial was not designed with sufficient power to draw statistical conclusions about individual sub- groups. Thus, one should be cautious in interpret- ing the results of subgroup analyses.

criticisms.text: Increased incidence of serious hyperkalemia with eplerenone; need to monitor serum potassium and adjust dose accordingly.
criticisms.quote: There was an increased incidence of serious hy- perkalemia among patients assigned to eplerenone.
